before-shield-of-arrav-is-started.text: If talking to Reldo for the first time ever:

steps.npc: Hello, stranger.

steps.player: Hello there! The name's [player name]. Who are you?

steps.npc: My name is Reldo. I'm the palace librarian.

steps.player: Ah, that explains why you're in the library then.

steps.npc: Well, truth be told, I would probably be here even if it wasn't where I worked. I very much like reading, not to mention sharing what I learn with all who are interested.

steps.player: Sounds like a very noble goal!

steps.npc: Hello there, [player name].

options.text: I'm in search of a quest.

steps.player: I'm in search of a quest.

steps.npc: Hmm... I don't believe there are any here.
Let me think actually...
Ah, yes. I think I have something, if you're definitely interested?

steps.text: If the player's combat level is less than 10.
Before starting this quest, be aware that you combat level is lower than the recommended level of 10.

steps.prompt: Start the Shield of Arrav quest?

steps.player: Of course.

steps.npc: Well, if you look around for book called The Shield of Arrav, you'll find a quest in there.
I'm not sure where the book is mind you... but I'm sure it's around here somewhere.

steps.player: Great! Thank you.
Actually, I don't think I am. Goodbye.

before-shield-of-arrav-is-started.text: If the player has a message for him:

options.text: The Wise Old Man of Draynor Village sent you this message.

steps.player: The Wise Old Man of Draynor Village sent you this message.

steps.npc: Ah, I am always delighted to hear from him. You would not imagine the depths of his wisdom!

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space for a reward:

steps.npc: I'd give you a reward, but you don't seem to have any space for it. Come back when you do.

steps.text: If the player has at least one inventory space for a reward:
Reldo gives you some coins.
some coins

steps.npc: King Roald has been very generous with my salary, so I can spare you some coins for your trouble.

steps.text: Reldo gives you some seeds.
assorted seeds

steps.npc: These little things seem to be everywhere these days! Perhaps you'd like them?

steps.text: Reldo gives you some runes.
assorted runes

steps.npc: My old friend Aubury sent me some runes in return for some books he wanted. Perhaps you'd like them?

options.text: Do you have anything to trade?
Do you have anything to trade?
I'm in search of a quest.
options.condition: If Shield of Arrav has not been started:

options.text: What do you know about the Imcando dwarves?

steps.player: What do you know about the Imcando dwarves?

steps.npc: The Imcando dwarves, you say? Let's see...
Ah, yes... For many hundreds of years, they were the world's most skilled smiths. They used secret smithing knowledge passed down from generation to generation.
Unfortunately, about a century ago, the once thriving group was wiped out during the barbarian invasions of that time.
I believe a few of them survived, but with the bulk of their population destroyed, their numbers dwindled even further. If any are left now, they'll no doubt keep to themselves.
However, I have heard tales of their love for redberry pie. Perhaps one of those could convince one to reveal their true heritage.

steps.player: So I just go around offering random dwarves redberry pie?

steps.npc: Well, not totally random. Apparently some of the surviving Imcando made a home for themselves near the cliffs on the Asgarnian southern peninsula. That would be a good place to start.

options.text: Do you have anything to trade?

steps.player: What can you tell me about this brooch?

steps.npc: I've never seen that symbol before. Where did you find it?

steps.player: In a cave beneath Lumbridge.

steps.npc: Very odd. Have you any idea how it got there?

steps.player: A goblin might have dropped it.

steps.npc: I've never heard of a goblin carrying a brooch like this. But just a minute...
The other day I filed a book about ancient goblin tribes. It's somewhere at the west end of the library, I think. Maybe that will be of some use.

options.text: Do you have anything to trade?
I have a cat related question.

steps.player: I have a cat related question.

steps.npc: Yes?

steps.player: Well...

steps.text: If the player isn't wearing an amulet of catspeak:

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Meow.

steps.player: Hmm... My cat is trying to say something but I'm not wearing the Amulet of Catspeak.

steps.text: If the player is wearing an amulet of catspeak:

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Go on... ask him.

steps.player: Okay, okay. I'm on it.
Do you know anything about Robert the Strong?

steps.npc: Ah, Robert the Strong. There's some details on him in one of my books on the history of Gielinor. Let's see now...
Fourth Age... Popular Lore... Ah here we are, Robert the Strong!
'Not much is known about the hero called Robert the Strong. Most folk tales describe him as being taller than the tallest human and far stronger than the strongest warrior.'
'He wields a six foot tall longbow and travels with his faithful panther, Odysseus. He is said to have had a personal crusade against the dragonkin...'

steps.player: Dragonkin?

steps.npc: I'm coming to that.
'The stories tell of the dragonkin being an intelligent race of bird-like creatures that walked rather than using their wings. They are said to be immortal, but cannot reproduce.'
'Because of this, they became very afraid of death and shunned all other races.'
'Some even say the dragonkin made corrupted versions of themselves for protection, what we now know as dragons. However, this has never been proven.'

steps.player: Hmm... Doesn't sound very believable.

steps.npc: There's no doubt that some elements of these tales have been overexaggerated for storytelling purposes, but you should be careful of outright dismissing them.
Robert the Strong is a name that often comes up in stories from the Fourth Age. There's no reason not to believe that these folk tales are based on events that actually happened.

steps.player: Thank you Reldo, you've been most... helpful.
That was a nice tale for mothers to tell their children, but I don't see how this helps Bob?

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Don't you think it's odd that no one knows where Bob came from?

steps.player: I guess, but he's just a cat... right?

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: I'd hoped you would've understood by now that there's more to cats than humans believe!

steps.player: Ok, ok! I get your point, after all I'm being dragged round Gielinor by... my cat!

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: I wouldn't say dragged... let's call it a partnership!

steps.player: Ok!
So are you saying that Robert the Strong is... is...
Bob?!

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Let's ask Bob!

steps.player: Let's go!

options.text: Do you have anything to trade?

steps.player: Hello. I was wondering if you could help me with something.

steps.npc: What do you need?

steps.player: I'm looking for information on a Fourth Age hero. His name was Tristan and he fought alongside Robert the Strong.

steps.npc: Ah you must mean Tristan Corvo. I can't remember anyone ever asking about him before, most prefer to hear about the bigger heroes like Arrav or Robert.

steps.player: But you know about Tristan?

steps.npc: Oh yes. What was it you wanted to learn?

steps.player: I'd like to learn about his descendants. I know they lived in this area.

steps.npc: Well we do have census records which date back to when the city was still called Avarrocka. I'm afraid we don't have anything from before that time though.

steps.player: Hmmm. It might still be worth a look. Where can I find this information?

steps.npc: I have a book around here somewhere with all of the details, why don't you see if you can find it. It's red if I remember right.
Have you found that book yet?

steps.text: If the player has found Varrock census records:

steps.player: I have it here.

steps.npc: Wonderful, let's have a look.

steps.player: So what does the book say?

steps.npc: Okay let's see... The Corvo family... Here we are! According to this there was a family by the name of Corvo living in Avarrocka for most of the Fourth Age.
The last entry is from the year 1770 of the Fourth Age.

steps.player: What happened to them?

steps.npc: Impossible to say for sure but it was around that time that many people left Misthalin to settle in Morytania. It's possible that the Corvo family was among them.
I'm afraid that's all the help I can provide. Port Phasmatys is where most of the Morytania settlers wound up. Perhaps you'll find what you're looking for there.

steps.player: Okay, thanks Reldo.

steps.text: If the player has found Varrock census records but dropped them:

steps.player: I found it but then I lost it.

steps.npc: You lost it?

steps.player: I'm sorry. I'm a terrible person.

steps.npc: Well you'd better find it again. These books are very valuable.

steps.text: If the player has not found Varrock census records:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.npc: I know it's around here somewhere. It's red if I remember right.

steps.player: Hello.

steps.npc: Did you have any luck finding the Corvo family?

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.npc: Port Phasmatys might be a good place to look. It's where most of the Morytania settlers wound up.

treasure-trails-beginner.text: If the player does not possess a strange device:

steps.player: Hi Reldo, I have come to ask you to help with something.

steps.npc: What can I do for you [player name]?

steps.text: You show Reldo your clue scroll.

steps.npc: Ah! Do you know about hot and cold clues?

steps.player: Yes, I do.

steps.npc: Well then use this strange device to feel where your destination is and dig.

steps.text: If the player has enough inventory space:
Strange device
If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.npc: You should make some room for it before I can give you it.

steps.player: No, I don't.

steps.npc: Ah, you use a strange device to tell you how far away you are from the place you need to be. When you get to your destination you dig.
Well then use this strange device to feel where your destination is and dig.

steps.text: If the player has enough inventory space:
Strange device
If the player does not have enough inventory space:

steps.npc: You should make some room for it before I can give you it.

treasure-trails-beginner.text: If the player possesses a strange device:

steps.player: Hey Reldo, I have one of those clue scrolls again, do you have any advice?

steps.npc: That strange device will guide you in the same way the key did. Feel it, but be careful as it is very powerful. Good luck.

9ea2nP.player: Do you have anything to trade?
How much do you want for that then?

9ea2nP.npc: No, sorry, that was just my little joke. I'm not the trading type.

WJxZYR.player: Ah. That's why you're in the library then.

WJxZYR.npc: Although I would probably be in here even if I didn't work here. I like reading. Someday I hope to catalogue all of the information stored in these books so all may read it.
